rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 55 (Watch-fors): 'Don't pre-empt the three-pattern (reference / plan.md / verifier). The pre-read names failure modes, not fixes. Naming the fixes here collapses the M5 contrast.' Commit 1e4ae21 correctly swept the three substantive dual-wired/M4-pre-read restatements (lines 38, 40, 52 in the current file) to the corrected in-room-M5-opener fact, and I grepped the whole corpus (learn-from-the-test.md, trainer-modules.md, learning-through-contrast.md, vocabulary.md) and found every OTHER inbound reference already reads 'in-room opener, not a pre-read' — but this fourth, self-referential use of 'the pre-read' as this file's own identifying label survived the sweep, four lines below the corrected 'Delivery mode: In-room M5 opener... do not re-file it as prework' line. Harm the rule guards: a stale duplicated fact rots silently and misleads the next editor into re-deriving or re-instating a design already proven wrong — which is exactly the failure this file already suffered once (three prior restatements of the same wrong premise). Harm is present but attenuated here: the substantive claim (WHEN this fires, i.e. M4 close vs M5 open) is not restated wrong — the corrected Delivery-mode line sits directly above and is the block's most prominent, first-read statement — and the sentence's actual content (this file names modes, not fixes) stays true regardless of the label. Non-blocking: this is a terminology echo of a retired self-descriptor, not a re-assertion of the disproven M4-Debrief/dual-wired premise itself.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Swap the self-reference from 'The pre-read' to a label consistent with the corrected Delivery-mode line — e.g. 'This lecture names failure modes, not fixes' or 'The opener names failure modes, not fixes' — so the maintainer block doesn't call itself a pre-read four lines after stating it explicitly is not one.
